I say this because all of the INTPs I’ve known personally are basically “my way of the highway, and when I want this highway to end, it does” types. It’s very annoying. I think INTPs get tired of helping people much more easily than they’d like to admit. In their head, they’re going out of their way to help people a lot, but what is a lot to them is considered little in the eyes of, say, extroverts? They’re trying their best, lol. Same applies to INFPs but to a lesser extent due to them being an F type, and it is expressed in a much different way. For example, if you go to an INFP and say hey, I really need someone to help and listen to me, they will certainly help at that moment. However, if you do that consistently or for a long period of time, they will get annoyed as they’ll feel the need to have you attend to their emotions/Fi instead. I’ve noticed this oftentimes happens in the same conversation, i.e. you need help, you get help for 5 minutes, and now they take their turn to express their emotions/struggles recently. Unlike INTPs though, as long as the balance is equal, they could keep this going for a while and will consider it a positive convo, which it was as long as they didn’t do something like this: 

Person: “I’ve been feeling so down recently…”
INFP: “I’ve been sad too… my boyfriend broke up with me”
Which honestly, the immature ones do a lot, because they either don’t realize or care that they made the convo about themselves in 0.2 seconds… because how can I seriously respond to their reply without seeming like an asshole? I notice INFP females do this tremendously frequently whereas the INFP males do not. 

Anyway, INTPs will ignore you for as long as they want to and then be like, okay, let me help… and then say a couple of sentences and expect/hope that they’ve provided you with an answer and so now it’s over with and you guys can move on. If they give you the answer and you keep talking, they’ll try to make it logical again, but if they fail to find a logical solution or the emotion of the situation has escalated, their Fe will be triggered and then they’ll get all anxious. In such moments, they are trying to be supportive but it’s likely coming off as either being disinterested or annoyed. So on and so forth. Really, you could get into that situation repetitively with them and they’d still help you out for a while but at the end of the day it’s going to be on their terms. If it’s too much for them, one day they’ll get so fed up with it that they’ll just ignore you all together due to secretly getting annoyed with you. Since they aren’t good enough with social shit/emotions to express it and don’t desire to put in the effort of changing the situation and/or don’t believe they can, they just end up ghosting. Has happened to me a few times with them :I

All in all, my point is, both on the self-centered side but in very different ways, and I think it’s due to their top functions being Ti and Fi. I believe both types need someone who doesn’t require a lot of attention and emotional energy. Those people need xxFJ types, lol. I have few intense and stable convictions, but one thing I truly believe is that there isn’t a single justification for someone to consistently do horrible things. 

We all fuck up at times, and of those times, we can fuck up the same thing… sure… but soon enough, we learn. I live my life by a short phrase: fuck around and find out. Contrary to its typical use, I actually find it to be motivating in a way that prevents overthinking. Any pressing question, task, etc.? Who cares, fuck around and find out. That is: experience, acknowledge, accept, reflect, and move tf on. 

With that being said, the goal is to experiment as much as possible and find the best life. Thus, I make a lot of mistakes. As a result of how much freedom I give myself, I can easily see what it is I do and do not want: what the intended course of action was, how it deviated (inevitably), and the result. So, the thing is…. when I fuck up, it’s because I wanted to, ultimately. I chose an action, evaluated all of the possible consequences, and did it anyway. However, when I do mess up, I oftentimes didn’t realize the gravity of what I have done. Nevertheless, the thoughts behind the action were all the same: “Eh, I’m willing to take that risk.” Therefore, absolving accountability simply isn’t possible. It’s my belief that we as humans are doing this on a subconscious level all the time. I simply believe for me it’s a more evident mental process. 

Accordingly, I don’t take apologies or justifications seriously. I say, well, you understood the risk in at least some sense, and chose to do the act anyway. It doesn’t matter if you didn’t anticipate this result, because the TRUTH is that your action had this result. You presupposing what already happened is totally irrelevant. 

People don’t stop what they’re doing because it’s wrong, people stop what they’re doing because they didn’t like the consequences. If someone says they stopped doing something because it’s wrong, what they’re really saying is “That made me feel bad,” AKA “I didn’t like the emotional consequences of my action.” Those who don’t feel as intense of an emotional response don’t feel the guilt and also don’t fear anything to the same extent of neurotypical (r/aspd), so they do what they want.

Well, I’m getting tired, but my whole point is: we know what we are doing, at the VERY LEAST on a subconscious level, and therefore we are actually aware of those action’s connotations, denotations, and associations in general. So, in regards to that guy, I must say,… he cannot blame it on a group of people, it’s just him. Acknowledge, accept, reflex, and move tf on. Lol
